1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Felsheim for three days. In the spring, Anna Weber's elder sister had left for Berlin, and since then Anna had been running the village's small pharmacy alone.
At nightfall she closed the shutters, counted the day's takings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when there was a loud knocking at the door downstairs. A man's voice called out, "Is anyone there?"
At the door stood a young man, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a bloodied cloth. He introduced himself as Konrad Wolf and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need a bandage," Wolf said quietly. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred marks be enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oil paper from his jacket. "This letter has to be at Steinbach Monastery before the eighteenth of May."
Anna must have been blind — only now did she notice how pale he was.
Even so, she refused his money and simply said, "I'll take you into the mountains first thing in the morning."
2: At daybreak they set off. Anna carried a basket on her back containing bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up they met old Hans Becker chopping wood. He laid his axe aside and said quietly that three strangers had asked at the entrance to the village the previous evening about an injured young man.
"Take the trail, Anna," Hans Becker said. "The main road isn't safe." Anna thanked him.
The trail was narrow and slippery. Anna went ahead, placing each step carefully. Wolf followed her in silence.
Around midday the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and in the distance the roof of Steinbach Abbey came into view. At the gate stood a nun, Sister Hildegard, who welcomed guests at the abbey.
Sister Hildegard took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting 2 years for this letter."
Wolf said to Anna, "I owe you my life." Anna smiled. "Then next time you can fix the roof of my pharmacy." Wolf stayed at the abbey.
In the evening Anna came down the mountain alone. When she arrived home it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat for a long time behind the counter.
